claims.claim: Moral reality is load-bearing: people's responses to betrayal, cruelty, and justice are signals that the universe contains accountability beyond matter in motion.
claims.plain_english: When people get angry about unfairness, it shows that right and wrong are real things in the universe, not just opinions.
claims.evidence_given: The document points to universal human reactions of protest against betrayal and demands for justice as evidence.
claims.what_would_break_it: If moral outrage could be fully explained as a social or evolutionary illusion with no objective basis.

claims.claim: A true judge cannot dismiss guilt by pretending the wrong never happened.
claims.plain_english: If someone is really in charge of justice, they can't just ignore crimes and pretend they didn't happen.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts this as a logical consequence of taking justice seriously, without further empirical support.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a coherent system of justice could exist where a judge legitimately overlooks offenses without undermining justice itself.

claims.claim: If someone bears the cost, mercy can appear without erasing the offense.
claims.plain_english: Mercy is possible without pretending the bad thing didn't happen, as long as someone else pays the price.
claims.evidence_given: The document presents this as a logical link in a chain, but provides no examples or external evidence.
claims.what_would_break_it: If there is no coherent mechanism by which a substitute can bear the moral or legal cost of an offense.

claims.claim: A closed system cannot generate the term it needs to heal itself from decay.
claims.plain_english: If a system is broken, it can't fix itself from the inside—it needs help from outside.
claims.evidence_given: The document states this as a principle without elaboration or examples.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a real-world example exists of a closed system that spontaneously generated a solution to its own fundamental decay.

claims.claim: The Gospel is not an escape from justice. It is justice and mercy meeting without collapse.
claims.plain_english: The Christian message isn't about getting out of being punished—it's about how fairness and forgiveness can both happen at the same time.
claims.evidence_given: The document presents this as the conclusion of the six-link chain, but provides no scriptural or historical evidence.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the Gospel can be shown to be fundamentally an escape from justice, or if justice and mercy cannot logically coexist in the way described.

claims.claim: If morality is real, then the universe contains more than matter in motion. It contains accountability.
claims.plain_english: If right and wrong are real, then the universe isn't just made of stuff moving around—it also has a system of responsibility.
claims.evidence_given: The document uses the pull quote to assert this as a consequence of moral realism.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a purely materialistic account of the universe can fully explain moral accountability without invoking anything beyond matter.
